title: Can a number ever be less than zero?
description: A winter morning in Leh, a deep well and a borrowed sum of money show three ways to have less than zero of something. The video names these numbers negative numbers.
teaching_notes: One idea: numbers continue past zero to the other side, and these are called negative numbers. Watch for the slip of thinking zero means nothing, so nothing can be below it.

source: Can there be a number less than 0? Can you think of any ways
video_script.why: The child accepts that numbers go on below zero, and meets three everyday cases: a cold temperature, a place under the ground, and money owed.
video_script.substitution: Treat zero as a mark on a line and ask what lies on the other side of that mark.
video_script.anchor: A thermometer on a winter morning in Leh, with the red line dropping under the zero mark
video_script.wrong_answer: nothing is less than zero, because zero means nothing is there
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu says nothing is less than zero, because zero means nothing is there. The red line of the thermometer drops under the zero mark, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: Yes, there are numbers less than zero

final_answer.spoken: yes, there are numbers less than zero, for example the cold below zero, a place under the ground, and money owed

never_show: a rule for adding negative numbers
maths_rules: 0 is a mark on a line, not the end of the line
a temperature colder than 0 degrees is less than 0
a place under the ground is below level 0
money owed is less than 0 rupees in hand
a number less than 0 is called a negative number
your turn: money owed is less than 0, no numbers needed
video_script.design: One idea: there are numbers on the other side of zero. Assumes only counting. Wrong idea: zero means nothing so nothing is below it. Anchor stays all video; one clear before the recap.
